edges.description: PRKAR1A encodes the regulatory subunit of protein kinase A; a 2023 review states that losing its function leaves the catalytic subunit's activity unopposed.

A 2023 review states that the unopposed kinase promotes proliferation in cAMP-responsive cells, and in mice heterozygous Prkar1a loss gives Schwann cell tumours. The mouse tumours are not pigmented, so the model covers the growth of the tumour and not its melanin; how the kinase drives this tumour is not shown.
Growing on a spinal nerve root, the tumour forms a paraspinal mass that compresses the root and can compress the spinal cord.
The tumour metastasizes, in 11 of 26 patients with follow-up in the 2014 series; how it spreads is not shown.
Compression of the nerve root; a 2024 case report describes gradual compressive symptoms over months to years, as with schwannoma.
Pain, usually local, is the commonest presentation; how the tumour produces it is not established.
The mass can compress the spinal cord as well as the nerve root.

nodes.description: Spread to distant organs, typically the lung and pleura. In the 2014 series only a mitotic rate above 2 per 10 high-power fields correlated with metastasis.

nodes.description: The tumour: a clonal proliferation of Schwann cells that make melanin, arising from nerve roots. Electron microscopy shows Schwann cell features, long processes and a continuous basal lamina, together with melanosomes, and transcriptomic and proteomic analyses in a 2026 multi-omic study showed activation of the melanin-synthesis pathway.

evidence.snippet: It originates from nerve roots with clonal Schwann cell proliferation and melanin pigment production.

evidence.snippet: Ultrastructurally, the cells features elongated processes, continuous basal lamina, melanosomes, and intercellular long-spacing collagen.

nodes.description: A lesion often reported in this tumour: loss of function of PRKAR1A, which encodes the type 1A regulatory subunit of protein kinase A. A 2023 review states that somatic PRKAR1A loss-of-function mutations occur in both sporadic and Carney complex-associated tumours. How often it is found varies: in a 2026 conference abstract of 13 patients, 8 of the 11 sequenced cases had a PRKAR1A loss-of-function mutation, without saying whether germline or somatic; in the 2014 series PRKAR1A protein was lost in 7 of 20 tumours stained; and a 2025 case report's background notes that not all tumours show PRKAR1A loss and that sporadic tumours frequently retain its expression. In the Carney complex the predisposing lesion is usually a heterozygous germline PRKAR1A variant.

nodes.description: There is no standard of care; the accepted approach for a localized tumour is complete resection with negative margins. In a 2024 systematic review two thirds of published patients had gross total resection, and recurrence-free, metastasis-free and overall survival did not differ significantly between treatment approaches, though the review sees a trend favouring gross total resection alone or subtotal resection with radiotherapy over subtotal resection alone. In the Carney complex, GeneReviews lists surgery to remove primary and metastatic tumours.

evidence.reference_title: Malignant Melanotic Nerve Sheath Tumors: A Review of Clinicopathologic and Molecular Characteristics.
evidence.snippet: Owing to the rarity of disease and variability in reported outcomes, there is no standard of care when it comes to the management of MMNST. Nonetheless, the accepted treatment strategy generally involves complete surgical resection with negative margins for localized tumors.

evidence.reference_title: Surgical management of malignant melanotic nerve sheath tumors: an institutional experience and systematic review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: Most patients underwent gross-total resection (GTR) (n = 41, 66.1%), followed by subtotal resection (STR) (n = 12, 19.4%), STR with radiation therapy (9.7%), and GTR with radiation therapy (4.8%).

evidence.reference_title: Surgical management of malignant melanotic nerve sheath tumors: an institutional experience and systematic review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: Kaplan-Meier analyses showed no significant differences among treatment approaches in terms of recurrence-free, metastasis-free, and overall survival (p > 0.05).

evidence.reference_title: Surgical management of malignant melanotic nerve sheath tumors: an institutional experience and systematic review of the literature.

nodes.description: Without its regulatory subunit, the catalytic subunit of protein kinase A is active without restraint. Removing Prkar1a from cells raises PKA activity, as seen in tumours from patients with the Carney complex, and a 2025 case report's background says PRKAR1A loss has been proposed as a key event in this tumour, through dysregulated cAMP signalling.

evidence.reference_title: Use of mouse models to understand the molecular basis of tissue-specific tumorigenesis in the Carney complex.
evidence.snippet: At the biochemical level, removal of Prkar1a from cells causes enhanced PKA activity, the same effect which has been observed in tumours isolated from CNC patients.

evidence.reference_title: Cervical Malignant Melanotic Nerve Sheath Tumor with retained PRKAR1A expression and a clinically benign course: a case report and review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: Loss of PRKAR1A expression has been proposed as a key molecular event in MMNST pathogenesis, leading to dysregulated cAMP signaling and tumorigenesis
